title: Falling card activity predicts churn
discovery: Customers whose transaction count fell by half from Q1 to Q4 churned at 50.9%. The portfolio rate is 16.1%.
evidence: 1,370 customers, lift 3.2. Transaction count has the strongest correlation with churn (r = -0.371). 23 of the 30 churn rules contain a low transaction count or a low count change. Source: phase9_insight_facts.json, models/rules.json.
recommendation: Compute the Q4/Q1 transaction ratio each month. Open a retention case when the ratio is below 0.5.

title: Unused credit lines churn most
discovery: Customers with a zero revolving balance churned at 36.1%. Customers with a balance of $1,000 to $2,000 churned at 4.6%.
evidence: 2,470 customers, lift 2.25. High utilization (above 0.75) churned at 15.5%, which is below the portfolio rate. 8 of the 30 churn rules contain a low balance and low utilization. Source: phase9_insight_facts.json, models/rules.json.
recommendation: Flag a card that has a zero balance for two statements. Offer a balance transfer or an instalment plan.

title: Inactive customers with low use churn at 47%
discovery: Customers with 3 or more inactive months and a low transaction count churned at 46.8%.
evidence: 1,241 customers, lift 2.9. Inactivity alone is weaker: 4 or more inactive months gives 24.6%. 9 of the 30 churn rules contain inactivity above 2.5 months. Source: phase9_insight_facts.json (combos), models/rules.json.
recommendation: Start a re-engagement message at the second inactive month. Call the customer at the third month if the transaction count is low.

title: Many bank contacts signal distress
discovery: Customers who contacted the bank 5 times in a year churned at 33.5%. Customers with no contacts churned at 1.8%.
evidence: Contact count has the strongest positive correlation with churn (r = +0.204). 10 of the 30 churn rules contain more than 2.5 contacts. Source: phase9_insight_facts.json, models/rules.json.
recommendation: Send customers with 4 or more contacts to a resolution desk. Record the reason for each contact.

title: Customers with 1 or 2 products churn twice as often
discovery: Customers with 1 or 2 products churned at 25.6% and 27.8%. Customers with 6 products churned at 10.5%.
evidence: The two churn rules with the highest lift (5.9, confidence 95%) contain a product count of 3 or less. RandomForest importance rank 7. Source: phase9_insight_facts.json, models/rules.json.
recommendation: Sell a second product in the first year. Track churn by product count.

title: One segment holds 64% of all churn
discovery: The At-Risk Mid-Tier segment has 39% of customers and 63.8% of all churned customers. Its churn rate is 26.1%.
evidence: K-means, k = 3, selected by silhouette (0.218). Segment profile: credit limit $6,486, revolving balance $498, 60 transactions per year. Source: phase9_insight_facts.json (byCluster).
recommendation: Put the retention budget in this segment. A decrease from 26% to 21% keeps about 200 customers per year.

title: Premium Loyal customers use 7% of their credit
discovery: The Premium Loyal segment has the highest credit limit ($24,287) and uses 6.8% of it. Its churn rate is 11.7%.
evidence: 1,920 customers. They spend the most: $6,737 per year in 75 transactions. Source: phase9_insight_facts.json (byCluster).
recommendation: Offer rewards and instalment purchases to increase card use. Do not spend the retention budget here.

title: Card colour does not predict churn. Value score does.
discovery: Blue cards churned at 16.1% and Silver cards at 14.8%. The Bronze value tier churned at 30.4% and the Gold tier at 7.7%.
evidence: Income, education, gender and marital status are all within 2 points of the portfolio rate. Source: phase9_insight_facts.json.
recommendation: Segment retention campaigns by value score and activity. Do not segment by card colour or demographics.
